detail.problem: extraction target has no anchor; its value cannot be relocated on a fresh page

detail.reason: The navigation half of this capability records cleanly: search "bath towels" from the storefront search box, then set the "Sort by" combobox to "Price: Low to High" so the first three result rows are by construction the three cheapest. What cannot be recorded is the output. Every price node fails extract() with "no anchor; its value cannot be relocated on a fresh page" — I tried (1) the price links in the results grid, (2) the bare price text immediately following the "Price, product page" label in a result row, and (3) the buy-box price on the product detail page (/dp/B0F93YTRV4), adjacent to "In Stock". On these screens only spec-table cells are anchored to stable labels (e.g. "Gray"->Color, "Generic"->Brand, "Cotton"->Material); prices are unanchored positional text. For a human's reference, today's sorted-ascending top three read $0.02 (2 Pack Microfiber Towel Set, In Stock), $0.69 (Soft Cotton Bath Towel Set) and $0.98 (Bath Towels, 3 Pack Coral Fleece) — but I am deliberately not committing these via extract(), because a recorded step that cannot relocate its target would either fail on replay or bind to whatever text occupies that grid position next time, silently returning a wrong price. Note also that the cheapest listings here are sub-$1 items with $7.99-$12.99 shipping, so "cheapest by item price" may not be the intended business meaning of cheapest.
detail.blocking: Need a price element that the extractor can anchor to a stable label. Options a human could decide on: expose the existing "Price, product page" label as a real anchor for the adjacent price text in each result row; or point me at a screen where price is rendered in a labelled row (e.g. an order-detail or item-details table with a "Price:" label) that I can drive to per product; or confirm that unanchored, position-based price extraction is acceptable for replay and I will re-record it with that caveat. Also please confirm whether "cheapest" should rank on item price or item price plus shipping.
